# 22-persist-article-digests — spec

## Observation

**O7** (2026-08-27): "Article drawer content isn't in Postgres." **C7:** cold-start
latency — every session rebuilds what a DB read would answer.

Ground truth from the live code (precedence rule 2 — code beats the observation's
wording): the article shell (title, url, body, description, summary, hero image)
**is already Postgres-backed** (`articles` table, specs 16/17), served DB-first by
`getClaudeArticles()` (`src/lib/scraper.ts:443`). The actual gap is the
**ArticleDigest score card** — the drawer's main content: generated by ~24 Claude
Sonnet calls, cached only in an in-memory `Map` (`src/lib/digest.ts:38`), so every
cold Vercel instance regenerates all of them (`maxDuration = 60` on
`/api/digest` exists for exactly this).

## Locked decision

**D6** (see `brain/00-system/00-decision-log.md`): persist digests in Postgres and
move generation into the ingest pipeline (cron-driven); `/api/digest` becomes a
pure DB read with **no** request-time generation. A missing digest (article newer
than the last ingest, first deploy) renders the existing description-excerpt
fallback in `ScoreCard` until the next ingest. Option rejected: request-time lazy
backfill (reintroduces the cold-start LLM burst being removed).

## Desired behavior

1. `articles` gains `digest JSONB` (null = none yet) and
   `digest_hash TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` — the djb2 content hash
   (title+body) at digest time, mirroring the `embedded_hash` pattern. Both
   `db/schema.sql` and `ensureSchema()` in `src/lib/db.ts` change together
   (contract: `contracts/schema.md` — `db/schema.sql` stays authoritative).
2. Ingest (`scrapeAndPersist()` in `src/lib/scraper.ts`) digests stale articles
   (stored `digest_hash` ≠ current content hash) with bounded concurrency and
   persists non-null results immediately. Failures leave `digest_hash`
   unchanged so the next ingest retries; a digest failure never blocks ingest.
3. `GET /api/digest` reads persisted digests from Postgres and returns
   `{ digests: Record<url, ArticleDigest> }` — response shape unchanged for the
   client (`AppShell.tsx:173` consumes it as-is; missing keys already handled).
   No Anthropic client in the request path; `maxDuration = 60` removed.
4. No DB configured (`DATABASE_URL`/`POSTGRES_URL` unset) → `/api/digest`
   returns `{ digests: {} }`; the drawer degrades to fallback cards, matching
   the repo-wide "optional keys degrade gracefully" rule (D1).

## Outcome (what this buys the user)

A cold instance opens the article drawer from a single Postgres read — no LLM
burst, no 60s worst case. Cold-start C7 is closed for the drawer.

## Out of scope

- Remaining O1 surface: cold-start of the *article list itself* when the DB is
  empty/stale (self-heal scrape path) — O1 stays open for that.
- Digest backlog telemetry in `kb_meta` (YAGNI at ~24 articles).
- Any UI change (`src/components/**` untouched; fallback card already exists).
- Prod seeding is operational, not code: after merge, one authenticated hit of
  `/api/scrape/refresh` (or the next 06:00 cron) fills the digests.

## Alert rules tripped

**A2** (data schema): PR parks for human review before merge. A3 not tripped (no
UI files). A4 not tripped (no retrieval/prompt/citation change — the digest
prompt moves call sites, its text is unchanged).

## Known tension (for the record)

Harness law says "never mock the project's own modules", but the repo's existing
sanctioned suites (`scraper.db.test.ts`) mock `@/lib/db` and `@/lib/embedArticles`
by convention. The plan follows the established per-file convention when
extending existing test files; new tests mock only system boundaries
(`postgres`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`).
